answer: Submissions that land within 143 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The basalt detector writes to umber, and ivory makes public every merge. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, and thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 138 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 26 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
